key_insight: Indoor photovoltaics paired with (anti)ferroelectric materials could enable low-power edge AI by co-creating local energy harvesting, storage, and in-memory computation.
engineering_relevance: The paper frames a practical path to distributed intelligence by matching indoor-generated power with ultra-low-energy neuromorphic hardware, reducing reliance on centralized data centers and communication-heavy computation.
method: Assess indoor photovoltaic requirements for distributed intelligence
Compare emerging materials against energy-harvesting and low-power computing needs
Argue for (anti)ferroelectrics as a dual-use platform for storage and neuromorphic devices
evidence_signal: This is a perspective article synthesizing the field rather than reporting new experimental datasets, so its support comes from requirements analysis and materials comparison.
watch_item: Real-world deployment still depends on closing gaps in indoor PV performance, device reliability, and system integration across harvesting, storage, and computation.
paper_title: Computing at the Edge Enabled by Indoor Photovoltaics and Ferroelectrics
